slot.brief: Find local maxima/minima of a cubic or a trig-rational function: differentiate, solve f'(x)=0, classify with sign of f''

stem: For $x\ne 0$, the function $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^4+3x^3-120x^2+7x}{x}$ has a local maximum at which value of $x$?

verdicts.working: For x≠0, f(x)=2x³+3x²−120x+7. Then f′(x)=6(x+5)(x−4), so the critical points are −5 and 4. Since f″(−5)=−54<0, x=−5 is a local maximum.

working:
$f(x)=2x^3+3x^2-120x+7$, so $f'(x)=6(x+5)(x-4)=0$ gives $x=-5,4$. Since $f''(x)=12x+6$, $f''(-5)=-54<0$ and $f''(4)=54>0$; hence the local maximum occurs at $x=-5$.

Independent check: For x≠0, f(x)=2x³+3x²−120x+7. Then f′(x)=6(x+5)(x−4), so the critical points are −5 and 4. Since f″(−5)=−54<0, x=−5 is a local maximum.
solution: For $x\ne 0$, $f(x)=2x^3+3x^2-120x+7$, so $f'(x)=6(x+5)(x-4)$. At $x=-5$, $f''(x)=12x+6=-54<0$, hence $f$ has a local maximum there.
